headline: 9 Bangladeshis killed in Kolkata hotel fire
summary: A devastating blaze at a five-story hotel in central Kolkata has claimed the lives of 9 Bangladeshis, with 6 others injured.
details: At least 9 Bangladeshis were killed and 6 others injured in a massive fire that broke out at a five-story hotel in the New Market area of central Kolkata on Tuesday night.
The fire started around 2:00 AM on the third floor, quickly filling the rooms with thick black smoke, suffocating guests who were asleep during the blaze.
Local residents initially attempted rescue efforts before fire services arrived. Victims were rushed to the hospital, but 9 were declared dead on arrival.
The hotel lacked basic fire safety measures, including adequate water supplies, modern extinguishers, and emergency exits, with narrow stairs making evacuation difficult.
Police have sealed the hotel, and while a short circuit is suspected, preliminary reports suggest an air conditioner explosion may have caused the fire.
Forensic experts and senior Kolkata Police officials are investigating the site to confirm the exact cause of and identify the victims.
caption:
9 Bangladeshis killed in a Kolkata hotel fire. The victims were suffocated by smoke while they slept.

At least 9 Bangladeshis were killed and 6 others injured in a massive fire that broke out at a five-story hotel in the New Market area of central Kolkata on Tuesday night.

The fire started around 2:00 AM on the third floor, quickly filling the rooms with thick black smoke, suffocating guests who were asleep during the blaze.

Local residents initially attempted rescue efforts before fire services arrived. Victims were rushed to the hospital, but 9 were declared dead on arrival.

The hotel lacked basic fire safety measures, including adequate water supplies, modern extinguishers, and emergency exits, with narrow stairs making evacuation difficult.

Police have sealed the hotel, and while a short circuit is suspected, preliminary reports suggest an air conditioner explosion may have caused the fire.

Forensic experts and senior Kolkata Police officials are investigating the site to confirm the exact cause of and identify the victims.

headline: Legal challenge filed to stay presidential election scheduled for Thursday
summary: A Supreme Court lawyer has petitioned the Appellate Division to halt the polls, challenging the constitutional validity of Article 70.
details: Supreme Court lawyer Md Eunus Ali Akond has filed a petition with the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court seeking a stay on the presidential election scheduled for August 20.
This follows a High Court order that had previously cleared the way for the election to proceed, rejecting a similar writ petition filed by the same lawyer.

The legal challenge centers on the validity of Article 70 of the Constitution, which states that a parliamentary seat becomes vacant if a lawmaker resigns from or votes against their nominating party.

The High Court previously observed that the presidential election schedule was lawfully announced under the Presidential Election Act, 1991, and that any decision on Article 70 should be handled by a special parliamentary committee.
Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal has stated that there is currently no legal bar to holding the election on Thursday.
The new president is expected to take the oath of office on Friday evening if the election proceeds as scheduled.
caption:

The legal challenge centers on the validity of Article 70 of the Constitution, which states that a parliamentary seat becomes vacant if a lawmaker resigns from or votes against their nominating party.

The High Court previously observed that the presidential election schedule was lawfully announced under the Presidential Election Act, 1991, and that any decision on Article 70 should be handled by a special parliamentary committee.

Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal has stated that there is currently no legal bar to holding the election on Thursday.

The new president is expected to take the oath of office on Friday evening if the election proceeds as scheduled.
